doc_summary: `native_block_neighbor_changed(ticks, dimension, pos, state, changed, from, moved, handled)` runs on the server when a mod's block (one outside `minecraft:`) hears that a neighbour changed, in the level's own order of neighbour updates, after `native_neighbor_changed` observed it: 1.21.1's `BlockBehaviour.neighborChanged(state, level, pos, changed, from, moved)`, `changed` naming the block that changed and `from` where the update comes from (the block that changed, or the one passing the update on, as 1.21.1 hands it: 26.3 dropped it). Unlike the observation, it may change blocks and schedule ticks through `ticks`, as a lamp, a door or a redstone-driven machine does when the signal beside it changes; updates its changes cause run after it, as vanilla queues them. Set `handled` to skip what the block's template would do. Bundles need "hooks": @API:block_neighbor_changed@.
